patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches show a login form with text-entry fields and a primary action area; although these are username/password rather than search, the only relevant input-interaction taxonomy item besides validation is field behavior on entry and submit. The desktop sketch clearly shows two horizontal input boxes and a button, and the mobile sketch implies the same login form from the reference context.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: If interpreted strictly from the sketches plus reference context, the fields need JS only insofar as submit handling, focus states, and possibly Enter-key submission are managed. This is better represented by form validation, so this pattern is likely not truly intended.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop sketch explicitly depicts a compact login form with two text fields, a checkbox, and a submit button. The mobile sketch, while more abstract, corresponds to the same page and implies a login form adapted to a smaller viewport. Any login form with required credentials and submit action implies client-side validation and submission-state handling.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Validate required username/email and password before submit, support Enter-key submission, preserve checkbox state, and surface inline or summary errors if authentication fails or fields are empty. A loading/disabled submit state may also be needed during submission.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not show explicit error text, password reveal, or forgot-password flow behavior, so only baseline validation and submit handling are clearly implied.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a very low-JS page centered on authentication rather than rich interaction. The desktop view clearly shows a simple login form with two inputs, a checkbox, and a submit button; the mobile view appears to be the same content reflowed responsively. No navigation drawer, dropdowns, tabs, accordions, modal overlays, sticky elements, or infinite-loading behaviors are visibly indicated. The main JavaScript requirement across both viewports is robust form submission behavior with validation, focus handling, and accessible error feedback.
